scope_in: Names that assert only that the work is machine learning, deep learning or AI, and identify no sub-area, task, method or subject matter.
scope_out: A name that adds any qualifier with content ('Machine Learning for Genomics', 'Deep Learning Theory', 'Machine Learning Security') is not an umbrella label and goes to the branch named by the qualifier.
example_children: Machine Learning; Deep Learning; Artificial Intelligence
notes: 8.4% of paper-mentions (501/5990) land here, concentrated in 'Machine Learning' (249) and 'Deep Learning' (177). These are the two most frequent names in the corpus and they carry no information. Quarantining them is the single most important hygiene decision in this proposal: dumping them into any substantive branch would make that branch the largest in the report for no reason. Report this branch as a line, then exclude it from the area shares.

scope_in: Bare 'machine learning' labels and their trivial variants, including generic 'applied/methods-driven ML' phrasings.
scope_out: 'Machine Learning Theory' -> Learning Theory; 'Machine Learning Security' -> Adversarial Robustness; 'Machine Learning for X' -> the branch for X.
example_children: Machine Learning; Machine Learning Algorithms; Machine Learning Applications
notes: 249 papers on the bare name alone.

scope_in: Bare 'deep learning' and bare 'neural network' labels that name no architecture family, training question or application.
scope_out: 'Deep Learning Theory' -> Learning Theory; 'Recurrent Neural Networks', 'Transformers' -> Neural Architecture Design; 'Deep Reinforcement Learning' -> Reinforcement Learning.
example_children: Deep Learning; Neural Networks; Artificial Neural Networks
notes: 177 + 19 + 4 papers. The boundary with Neural Architecture Design is the presence of a named family.

scope_in: Bare 'artificial intelligence' labels, including AGI and 'intelligent systems' used as a field name.
scope_out: 'AI Safety', 'AI Ethics', 'Explainable AI' all have content and go to Trustworthy Machine Learning.
example_children: Artificial Intelligence; Artificial General Intelligence; Intelligent Systems
notes: Small (~18 papers) but must not be merged into General Machine Learning: some reports will want AI-as-a-field separated.

scope_in: Names that describe the shape of a piece of research rather than its subject: 'Algorithms', 'Theory', 'Empirical Study', 'Interdisciplinary Studies', 'Data Analysis'.
scope_out: 'Algorithm Convergence' -> Optimization Algorithms; 'Evaluation Methods' -> Evaluation Methodology; 'Theoretical Neuroscience' -> Neuroscience.
example_children: Algorithms; Interdisciplinary Studies; Empirical Study
notes: This is the proposal's only residual bucket. It holds ~25 paper-mentions (<0.5%). If an annotator is tempted to use it for anything else, the name belongs somewhere real.

scope_in: Research areas defined by how the learning problem itself is set up: what experience the learner receives, what it must produce, and across what it must generalize.
scope_out: Areas defined by the kind of data (text, images, graphs) -> Data-Modality Subfields; areas defined by a property the trained model must have (fair, private, robust) -> Trustworthy Machine Learning; the mathematics of the algorithm -> Formal Foundations of Machine Learning.
example_children: Reinforcement Learning; Self-Supervised Learning; Transfer Learning
notes: Largest ML branch in the corpus, driven by Reinforcement Learning (263). 10 children is at the rule-6 limit; each is a name the corpus uses hundreds or dozens of times and none subsumes another.

scope_in: Learning a policy from interaction with an environment that has state and transitions, including its variants, its algorithmic families, and its credit-assignment and exploration questions.
scope_out: Bandit problems with no state transitions -> Online Learning; control of a known dynamical system -> Control Theory; RL used as a tool on a robot -> Robotics if the name says 'robot', here if the name says 'RL'.
example_children: Deep Reinforcement Learning; Offline Reinforcement Learning; Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
notes: 263 papers on the bare name, plus ~120 distinct RL sub-names in the tail (option discovery, credit assignment, replay buffers, MDPs/POMDPs, policy gradients). By far the largest single research area in this corpus.

scope_in: Learning from labelled examples, and research on the supply and quality of those labels: semi-supervised, weak, active, noisy-label and class-imbalanced settings.
scope_out: Self-supervised pretext tasks -> Self-Supervised Learning; 'Image Classification' -> Computer Vision (the name commits to a modality, not to a supervision regime).
example_children: Semi-Supervised Learning; Active Learning; Learning with Noisy Labels
notes: The bare names ('Supervised Learning' 10, 'Classification' 5, 'Regression' 2) are thin; the category is carried by the label-efficiency tail.

scope_in: Learning from a signal constructed out of unlabelled data itself, including contrastive and non-contrastive objectives and masked prediction.
scope_out: What the learned features are for or what structure they should have -> Representation Learning; using a pretrained model on a new task -> Transfer Learning.
example_children: Contrastive Learning; Contrastive and Non-Contrastive Learning; Self-Supervised Learning (Graph Data)
notes: 73 + 21 papers. Kept separate from Representation Learning on purpose: SSL names a training signal, Representation Learning names a property of the output. Annotators will confuse them; the scope_out lines are load-bearing.

scope_in: Research on what a learned latent space should contain and how it is structured: disentanglement, identifiability, invariance, metric structure, dimensionality.
scope_out: The objective used to obtain it -> Self-Supervised Learning; a representation of a specific data type ('Graph Representation Learning', 'Protein Representation Learning') -> the modality or domain branch.
example_children: Disentanglement; Causal Representation Learning; Metric Learning
notes: 56 papers plus a large tail (manifold learning, object-centric representations, discrete representations, identifiability).

scope_in: Learning a distribution in order to sample from it, and the model families defined by how they do so.
scope_out: Generation of a specific medium named in the label ('Image Generation', 'Text-to-Image Synthesis', 'Molecule Generation') -> the modality or domain branch; likelihood-based inference without a sampler -> Probabilistic Inference.
example_children: Diffusion Models; Normalizing Flows; Generative Adversarial Networks
notes: 'Generative Models' (83) is the 7th most frequent name. This is the clearest case of an architecture word used as the name of a research problem; see the architecture policy in RATIONALE.md.

scope_in: Reusing or sharing what was learned on one task, domain, language or environment in another, including few-shot, zero-shot, domain adaptation, multi-task and meta-learning.
scope_out: Keeping old tasks while learning new ones over time -> Continual Learning; measuring degradation under a shift you did not choose -> Distribution-Shift Robustness.
example_children: Domain Adaptation; Few-Shot Learning; Meta-Learning
notes: Meta-Learning (26 papers) is folded in rather than made a sibling: the corpus contains only two other meta-* names, so a separate category would fail the three-example test. This is one of my least-certain calls.

scope_in: Learning a sequence of tasks over time without losing what was learned earlier.
scope_out: Transferring to one new task and stopping -> Transfer Learning; learning from a data stream with a regret objective -> Online Learning; deliberately removing knowledge -> Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning.
example_children: Catastrophic Forgetting; Lifelong Learning; Class-Incremental Learning
notes: 29 papers plus ~12 tail names. Boundary with Online Learning is task sequence vs sample stream.

scope_in: Training one model across parties that do not pool their data, and the communication, heterogeneity and aggregation problems that follow.
scope_out: Data-parallel training inside one cluster -> Machine Learning Systems Engineering; the privacy guarantee itself -> Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning.
example_children: Decentralized Learning; Communication-Efficient Learning; Byzantine Robustness
notes: 24 papers. Deliberately not merged with distributed training: the corpus treats them as different literatures.

scope_in: Deciding whether an input is unlike the training distribution or unlike normal operation, as the task being solved.
scope_out: Making a model perform well under shift rather than flagging it -> Distribution-Shift Robustness; detecting adversarially crafted inputs -> Adversarial Robustness.
example_children: Out-of-Distribution Detection; Outlier Detection; Time-Series Anomaly Detection
notes: 20 + 12 papers plus a tail (log-based, graph, fraud, misclassification detection). The near-homonym pair 'OOD Detection' (here) / 'OOD Generalization' (Trustworthy) is the highest-risk confusion in the whole structure.

scope_in: Learning from a stream of data or decisions under a regret or exploration objective, without a fixed training set.
scope_out: Interaction with a stateful environment -> Reinforcement Learning; convergence analysis of a batch optimizer -> Optimization Algorithms.
example_children: Multi-armed Bandits; Contextual Bandits; Online Convex Optimization
notes: Small (~15 paper-mentions) and added after the tail sample: 'Dynamic Learning', 'Concept Drift', 'Performative Prediction', 'Streaming SGD' had no home without it.

scope_in: The classical subfields of machine learning, each individuated by the kind of data it works on rather than by the method it uses or the science it serves.
scope_out: The scientific or professional subject that supplies the data ('Medical Imaging', 'Neuroimaging', 'Remote Sensing') -> the domain branch; the learning setup used ('Self-Supervised Learning') -> Learning Problem Formulations.
example_children: Natural Language Processing; Computer Vision; Graph Machine Learning
notes: Holds the two largest names in the corpus (NLP 295, CV 240). The head rule matters here: a name that pairs a modality with a science ('Medical Image Segmentation') is filed under the science, because the survey is being read by an institute that wants to know how much clinical work it does.

scope_in: Machine learning over human language in text form: tasks, language models, multilinguality, and the linguistic behaviour of text models.
scope_out: Language as an object of linguistic study -> Linguistics; generating or analysing source code -> Software Engineering; modality-agnostic adaptation techniques (prompting, PEFT) -> Foundation Model Adaptation.
example_children: Machine Translation; Question Answering; Text Summarization
notes: 295 papers, the single most frequent name. LLM-specific names (language modeling, instruction tuning, RAG, chain-of-thought) sit here at depth 3 except where the technique is modality-agnostic.

scope_in: Machine learning over images, video, 3D geometry and rendered scenes.
scope_out: Images of a body or a specimen -> Medical Imaging; satellite and aerial imagery -> Environmental Monitoring; vision on a robot -> Robotics if the name says robot.
example_children: Image Classification; Object Detection; Semantic Segmentation
notes: 240 papers plus a very large tail (3D reconstruction, NeRF, rendering, video, image generation, point clouds). Computer Graphics (9) is included here; the corpus never separates them.

scope_in: Machine learning over acoustic signals of any kind: speech, music, environmental and bioacoustic sound.
scope_out: The linguistic content once transcribed -> Natural Language Processing; EEG/MEG and other biosignals -> Neuroscience.
example_children: Speech Recognition; Speech Enhancement; Music Information Retrieval (MIR)
notes: ~45 paper-mentions. Named 'Audio Processing' rather than 'Speech and Audio' to keep one concept per category; scope_in states explicitly that speech belongs here, because annotators will not assume it.

scope_in: Learning on data whose primary structure is a graph: node, edge and graph-level tasks, message passing, graph expressivity, dynamic and heterophilic graphs.
scope_out: Graphs as a combinatorial optimization instance (routing, TSP, SAT) -> Combinatorial Optimization; molecular graphs where the name says molecule -> Drug Discovery or Computational Chemistry.
example_children: Graph Neural Networks; Node Classification; Link Prediction
notes: 'Graph Neural Networks' (76) is classified here, not as an architecture: in this corpus it is used as the name of the field. Includes Graph Theory (6) and Spectral Graph Theory where used to analyse learning.

scope_in: Learning over ordered signals indexed by time: forecasting, temporal point processes, change points, sequence models over non-linguistic series.
scope_out: Detection framed as the task -> Anomaly Detection; a time series of brain, climate or market data where the name says so -> the domain branch.
example_children: Time Series Forecasting; Temporal Point Processes; Sequence Modeling
notes: ~30 paper-mentions. 'Sequence Modeling' (8) is placed here rather than in NLP; that is a judgement call and the quotes are split.

scope_in: Learning that must align or fuse two or more modalities, and the models and benchmarks defined by that pairing.
scope_out: A single modality with an auxiliary signal -> that modality; multi-omics data fusion -> Computational Biology.
example_children: Vision-Language Models; Visual Question Answering; Audio-Text Representation Learning
notes: 15 + 11 + 4 papers plus a tail. Vision-language dominates; audio-text and vision-touch exist but are rare.

scope_in: Finding, ranking or recommending items that satisfy a user's information need, over document, product, media or interaction data.
scope_out: Understanding a query's meaning as a language problem -> Natural Language Processing; the interface through which results are presented -> Human-Computer Interaction.
example_children: Recommender Systems; Learning to Rank; Entity Matching
notes: 19 + 16 papers. Weakest fit in this branch: its 'modality' is really a task shape. I keep it here rather than inventing a one-member branch, and flag it in RATIONALE.md.

scope_in: Research on how to build, train, adapt and shrink neural networks, stated independently of the data they are applied to.
scope_out: Why deep networks generalize, as mathematics -> Learning Theory; architectures specialised to one modality ('Vision Transformers') -> that modality; the hardware and pipelines that run training -> Machine Learning Systems Engineering.
example_children: Attention Mechanisms; Knowledge Distillation; Prompt Engineering
notes: Four children only, and that is honest: the corpus has a lot of deep-learning practice vocabulary but it clusters tightly into these four.

scope_in: Research about the architectural components and design principles of neural networks: attention, memory, modularity, equivariance by construction, architecture search.
scope_out: A family used as the name of a research area (Graph Neural Networks, Diffusion Models) -> its field; making an existing architecture smaller or faster -> Model Compression.
example_children: Attention Mechanisms; Neural Architecture Search; Mixture of Experts
notes: ~50 paper-mentions. This is the only category that is genuinely about architectures-as-architectures and therefore the only one that overlaps the project's separate architecture ontology. Report it flagged.

scope_in: The empirical business of getting a network to train: optimizers in practice, learning-rate and batch-size choices, initialization, regularization, training dynamics, scaling behaviour.
scope_out: Convergence proofs and rates -> Optimization Algorithms; generalization bounds -> Learning Theory.
example_children: Neural Network Optimization; Training Dynamics; Regularization Techniques
notes: Its boundary with Optimization Algorithms is the proposal's second-riskiest seam: 'practice vs proof'. Stated as: if the name mentions a network or a training run, it lands here.

scope_in: Reducing a trained model's size, latency or energy while keeping its behaviour: distillation, pruning, quantization, sparsity, efficient inference.
scope_out: Distributing training over machines -> Machine Learning Systems Engineering; environmental cost arguments -> Responsible AI.
example_children: Knowledge Distillation; Neural Network Pruning; Quantization
notes: ~45 paper-mentions across a dozen near-synonyms ('Model Compression', 'Network Compression', 'Efficient Deep Learning', 'Model Efficiency').

scope_in: Steering an already-pretrained large model without retraining it from scratch: prompting, in-context learning, parameter-efficient fine-tuning, instruction tuning, preference tuning, model merging.
scope_out: Transfer between small task-specific models -> Transfer Learning; what the adapted model should be safe or aligned with -> AI Safety.
example_children: Prompt Engineering; In-Context Learning; Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT)
notes: A 2024 cluster that did not exist in earlier corpora; ~35 paper-mentions, almost all in the one-paper tail. Placing RLHF here rather than under Reinforcement Learning is deliberate and arguable.

scope_in: The mathematics that learning algorithms are built out of and analysed with: optimization, probability, causality, geometry, strategic interaction, dynamics.
scope_out: Empirical recipes for training networks -> Deep Learning Methodology; the same mathematics applied to a named science ('Molecular Dynamics') -> that science.
example_children: Optimization Algorithms; Probabilistic Inference; Causal Inference
notes: Nine children. This branch is where an institute's theory strength shows up; 'Optimization' alone is 71 papers and 'Bayesian Inference' 19.

scope_in: Continuous optimization as an object of study: convexity, stochastic and first-order methods, convergence rates, variance reduction, distributed and bilevel formulations.
scope_out: Discrete or integer decision problems -> Combinatorial Optimization; tuning a training run -> Neural Network Training; hyperparameter search as a service -> Evaluation Methodology.
example_children: Convex Optimization; Stochastic Optimization; First-Order Methods
notes: 'Optimization' (71) is the 10th most frequent name and its quotes are overwhelmingly continuous-optimization. ~60 further tail names (mirror descent, Polyak stepsize, variational inequalities, minimax).

scope_in: Discrete decision problems and the algorithms that solve them: integer programming, routing, scheduling, constraint programming, and learned heuristics for them.
scope_out: The industry that poses the problem ('Public Transport', 'Personnel Scheduling' as a workforce topic) -> Transportation Systems or Industrial Engineering; continuous relaxations studied for their own sake -> Optimization Algorithms.
example_children: Mixed Integer Programming; Vehicle Routing Problem; Job-Shop Scheduling
notes: 17 papers on the bare name plus 'Operations Research' (19) and ~40 tail names. Also the home for decision-focused / predict-then-optimize names such as 'Contextual Optimization' and 'Prescriptive Analytics'.

scope_in: Formal statements about what can be learned and how well: generalization bounds, sample complexity, expressivity, identifiability, and the theory of deep networks.
scope_out: Measured generalization gaps in experiments -> Neural Network Training; guarantees about a specific trained network -> Neural Network Verification.
example_children: Generalization Bounds; PAC-Bayesian Theory; Statistical Learning Theory
notes: Includes 'Machine Learning Theory' (8), 'Deep Learning Theory' (7), 'Theoretical Machine Learning' (5) and information-theoretic names; ~45 paper-mentions.

scope_in: Computing or approximating posteriors and likelihoods: Bayesian inference, variational methods, Monte Carlo, graphical models, density estimation, simulation-based inference.
scope_out: Learning a sampler as the research goal -> Generative Modeling; predicting a calibrated confidence for a downstream decision -> Uncertainty Quantification.
example_children: Bayesian Inference; Variational Inference; Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC)
notes: 19 papers on 'Bayesian Inference' plus ~50 tail names. The seam with Generative Modeling is real (normalizing flows appear in both literatures); the rule is whether the name is about inference or about sampling.

scope_in: Reasoning about interventions and counterfactuals: causal discovery, treatment-effect estimation, structure identifiability, causal representations.
scope_out: Correlational prediction in an applied field -> that field; epidemiological study design -> Public Health.
example_children: Causal Discovery; Causal Representation Learning; CATE Estimation
notes: 16 + 8 + 6 papers plus ~20 tail names. A distinct and visible cluster in this corpus, not a sub-branch of statistics.

scope_in: Strategic interaction between multiple decision makers: equilibria, cooperative and non-cooperative games, mechanism design, multi-agent systems as a formalism.
scope_out: Multi-agent reinforcement learning as a training method -> Reinforcement Learning; auctions as an economic subject -> Economics.
example_children: Multi-Agent Systems; Cooperative Game Theory; Coordination Games
notes: 20 + 11 papers. Placed under foundations rather than with RL because its quotes are about equilibrium analysis, not about learning algorithms.

scope_in: Geometric and topological structure used as a modelling principle: symmetry and equivariance, manifolds, optimal transport, spectral and kernel geometry.
scope_out: An equivariant architecture named as an architecture -> Neural Architecture Design; 3D scene geometry -> Computer Vision.
example_children: Geometric Deep Learning; Optimal Transport; Manifold Learning
notes: 11 + 8 + 4 papers plus ~25 tail names (scattering transforms, statistical manifolds, Lorentz invariance in a learning sense, equivariance).

scope_in: Driving a dynamical system to a desired behaviour with stability guarantees, and identifying such systems: optimal control, MPC, Lyapunov analysis, system identification.
scope_out: Learning a controller by trial and error -> Reinforcement Learning; the robot or grid being controlled -> Robotics or Energy Systems.
example_children: Model Predictive Control; Optimal Control; Dynamical Systems
notes: ~40 paper-mentions. Sits under foundations because the corpus names it as a mathematics, not as an engineering discipline; a reviewer could reasonably move it to Applied Engineering Domains.

scope_in: Learning that embeds or replaces a numerical simulation: physics-informed networks, operator and PDE learning, surrogate models, differentiable simulation.
scope_out: The science the simulation is of -> Physical Sciences or Environmental Sciences; statistical inference from simulator outputs -> Probabilistic Inference.
example_children: Physics-Informed Neural Networks; Neural Operators; Partial Differential Equation Solvers
notes: ~25 paper-mentions. Small but methodologically distinct and it gives a clear home to a tail that would otherwise scatter across four branches.

scope_in: Research on properties a deployed model must have beyond accuracy: fairness, transparency, privacy, robustness, calibration, safety, and the norms governing its use.
scope_out: Accuracy on a benchmark -> Evaluation Methodology; making a model smaller -> Model Compression; detecting anomalies as the task -> Anomaly Detection.
example_children: Fairness in Machine Learning; Model Interpretability; Adversarial Robustness
notes: ~200 paper-mentions and the most internally differentiated non-domain branch in this corpus; nine children is justified because each is its own literature with its own venues.

scope_in: Measuring and mitigating disparate model behaviour across groups or individuals.
scope_out: Dataset-level imbalance treated as a label problem -> Supervised Learning; normative and legal argument about AI -> Responsible AI.
example_children: Algorithmic Fairness; Bias Mitigation; Intersectional Fairness
notes: 19 + 12 papers plus ~25 tail names, many of them near-duplicate phrasings ('Fairness in AI', 'Machine Learning Fairness', 'Fairness and Bias'). A strong institute signal.

scope_in: Explaining what a model computes or why it produced an output: attribution, concept-based and mechanistic analysis, surrogate explanations.
scope_out: Inherently simple statistical models used in an applied field -> that field; verifying a formal property -> Neural Network Verification.
example_children: Explainable AI; Mechanistic Interpretability; Feature Importance
notes: ~45 paper-mentions spread over a dozen synonyms (XAI, Explainability, Interpretable Machine Learning, Model Understanding).

scope_in: Protecting the data a model was trained on: differential privacy, inference and reconstruction attacks, unlearning, privacy-preserving computation.
scope_out: Not pooling data across sites as a training architecture -> Federated Learning; data governance policy -> Responsible AI.
example_children: Differential Privacy; Membership Inference Attacks (MIAs); Machine Unlearning
notes: ~25 paper-mentions.

scope_in: Behaviour of models under deliberately crafted inputs or poisoned training data, and defences against them.
scope_out: Degradation under naturally occurring shift -> Distribution-Shift Robustness; flagging outliers as the task -> Anomaly Detection.
example_children: Adversarial Attacks; Adversarial Training; Certified Robustness
notes: 13 + 9 papers plus ~25 tail names, including attacks on language models and model stealing.

scope_in: Keeping performance when test data differs from training data through no adversary: covariate, label and subpopulation shift, worst-group performance, spurious correlation.
scope_out: Adapting to a known target domain with target data -> Transfer Learning; detecting that a sample is out of distribution -> Anomaly Detection.
example_children: Out-of-Distribution Generalization; Covariate Shift; Worst-Group Generalization
notes: ~35 paper-mentions. The scope_out against Anomaly Detection has to be read by any annotator handling an 'OOD' name; the two names differ by one word and mean different literatures.

scope_in: Producing and validating a model's own statement of confidence: calibration, predictive intervals, conformal methods, ensembles as uncertainty estimators.
scope_out: Posterior computation as mathematics -> Probabilistic Inference; measurement uncertainty in a scientific instrument -> that science.
example_children: Uncertainty Estimation; Model Calibration; Conformal Prediction
notes: 12 + 5 papers plus ~20 tail names.

scope_in: Preventing capable systems from pursuing unintended objectives: alignment, specification gaming, safe exploration, constrained policies, risk from advanced systems.
scope_out: Normative, legal or societal analysis -> Responsible AI; robustness to attacks -> Adversarial Robustness; clinical patient safety -> Clinical Medicine.
example_children: AI Alignment; Safe Reinforcement Learning; Goal Misgeneralization
notes: ~25 paper-mentions. Separated from Responsible AI on a technical-vs-normative line, which is the standard split in this literature and is legible in the quotes.

scope_in: Normative, legal and societal treatment of AI: ethics, governance, regulation, transparency obligations, equity and environmental accountability of the field itself.
scope_out: A technical fairness metric -> Fairness in Machine Learning; a technical privacy mechanism -> Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning; an alignment technique -> AI Safety.
example_children: AI Ethics; AI Governance; AI Policy
notes: ~40 paper-mentions over ~30 near-synonymous phrasings of 'AI ethics'. The name is general enough to attract the whole branch, so the scope_out must be enforced; this is a known weak point.

scope_in: Proving properties of a trained model or of a program containing one, by formal methods.
scope_out: Empirical robustness evaluation -> Adversarial Robustness; testing conventional software -> Software Engineering.
example_children: Robustness Verification; Formal Methods in Machine Learning; Quantitative Verification
notes: Small (~15 paper-mentions) and kept rather than merged, because its methods are disjoint from the rest of the branch. Borderline by rule 3.

scope_in: How machine learning research is measured and resourced: the benchmarks and metrics it is judged on, the datasets it consumes, and the systems it runs on.
scope_out: The property being measured (fairness, robustness) -> Trustworthy Machine Learning; the modelling technique -> Deep Learning Methodology.
example_children: Benchmarking; Dataset Creation; MLOps
notes: ~110 paper-mentions. Only three children and no more: the corpus does not distinguish further, and splitting would produce parents with one real child.

scope_in: Benchmarks, metrics, protocols, statistical comparison and reproducibility of empirical ML claims.
scope_out: Evaluating a clinical intervention -> Public Health; evaluating fairness specifically -> Fairness in Machine Learning.
example_children: Benchmarking; Evaluation Metrics; Model Selection
notes: ~50 paper-mentions including 'Model Evaluation', 'Metric Evaluation', 'Benchmark Design', 'Open Science', 'Reproducibility in Medical Imaging'.

scope_in: Constructing, documenting, cleaning, augmenting and valuing the data that ML research runs on.
scope_out: The domain the data comes from -> that domain; privacy guarantees over the data -> Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning.
example_children: Dataset Creation; Synthetic Data; Data Augmentation
notes: ~45 paper-mentions. Data Augmentation (11) is placed here rather than under regularization because the corpus's augmentation names are mostly about producing data, not about a training penalty.

scope_in: The software and hardware machinery of training and serving models: frameworks, compilers, parallelism, accelerators, MLOps, edge deployment.
scope_out: Compressing the model itself -> Model Compression; not pooling the data -> Federated Learning; designing chips as a research subject -> Computer Hardware.
example_children: MLOps; Distributed Training; Hardware Acceleration
notes: ~30 paper-mentions. Placed under Experimental Methodology rather than Applied Engineering Domains because its subject is ML research infrastructure, not a client industry.

scope_in: Research whose subject is human health, clinical practice, the nervous system, or molecular and cellular biology.
scope_out: Ecology, biodiversity and non-human organismal biology -> Environmental Sciences; psychological and behavioural research without a clinical or neural subject -> Social Sciences; medical device engineering -> Applied Engineering Domains.
example_children: Neuroscience; Medical Imaging; Bioinformatics
notes: The largest application branch by a wide margin: roughly 700 paper-mentions, about 12% of the corpus, concentrated in neuroscience (84), medical imaging (48), bioinformatics (40) and a very deep clinical tail. It is given top-level status rather than being nested under a general 'sciences' node so that its sub-areas surface at the reportable depth.

scope_in: Research organised around a clinical specialty, disease, patient population or care process, including medical education and clinical decision making.
scope_out: Imaging as the object of study -> Medical Imaging; radiation dose and treatment physics -> Medical Physics; population-level disease burden -> Public Health.
example_children: Oncology; Psychiatry; Pediatric Surgery
notes: The single deepest tail in the corpus: ~200 one-paper names covering specialties (nephrology, hepatology, neonatology, geriatrics), diseases, care processes and medical education.

scope_in: Acquisition, reconstruction, segmentation and analysis of images of the body or of biological specimens.
scope_out: Images of the brain used to study brain function -> Neuroscience; dose calculation and radiotherapy planning -> Medical Physics; natural images -> Computer Vision.
example_children: Medical Image Segmentation; Radiomics; Diffusion MRI
notes: 48 + 10 + 8 papers plus a tail (microscopy, histology, endoscopy, ultrasound, PET). Boundary with Neuroscience is intent: modality development here, brain science there.

scope_in: Physics of diagnosis and treatment: radiation therapy planning, dosimetry, brachytherapy, radiation transport and detection, nuclear medicine.
scope_out: Image analysis for diagnosis -> Medical Imaging; oncology as a clinical specialty -> Clinical Medicine.
example_children: Radiation Therapy; Brachytherapy; Dosimetry
notes: 18 + 8 + 7 + 5 papers plus ~20 tail names. Unusually prominent for an ML corpus and unmistakably a local group; keeping it separate from Medical Imaging is important or it disappears.

scope_in: Research whose subject is the nervous system: its measurement, its computation, its disorders as neural phenomena, and its use as a model for learning systems.
scope_out: Cognition studied behaviourally without neural measurement -> Cognitive Science; psychiatric care delivery -> Clinical Medicine; brain-inspired hardware -> Computer Hardware.
example_children: Computational Neuroscience; Neuroimaging; Cognitive Neuroscience
notes: ~230 paper-mentions once the tail is counted (EEG/MEG/fMRI analysis, connectomics, brain encoding and decoding, NeuroAI, neural dynamics). The one application area in this corpus where influence runs both ways into ML.

scope_in: Computational analysis and modelling of biological molecules and systems: sequences, structures, expression, omics, networks.
scope_out: Wet-lab or organismal biology -> Experimental Biology; designing a therapeutic compound -> Drug Discovery; quantum-level molecular energetics -> Computational Chemistry.
example_children: Bioinformatics; Genomics; Protein Structure Prediction
notes: 40 + 33 + 26 papers plus a deep omics tail (single-cell, proteomics, transcriptomics, phylogenetics, regulatory networks). Bioinformatics and Computational Biology are treated as one category because the corpus uses them interchangeably.

scope_in: Biology whose subject is an organism, tissue, cell or immune system rather than a computation over biological data.
scope_out: Sequence or expression analysis -> Computational Biology; ecology and biodiversity -> Ecology.
example_children: Immunology; Virology; Structural Biology
notes: ~35 paper-mentions. Thin and somewhat heterogeneous; a reviewer might fold it into Computational Biology, at the cost of making that category mean 'all biology'.

scope_in: Finding and designing therapeutic molecules: property prediction, generation, synthesis planning, binding, repurposing, response prediction.
scope_out: Materials and catalysts -> Materials Science; protein structure as a biology question -> Computational Biology.
example_children: Molecular Property Prediction; Retrosynthetic Planning; Drug Response Prediction
notes: ~30 paper-mentions. Separated from Computational Chemistry because its objective is therapeutic, which is how the quotes read.

scope_in: Health at population scale: epidemiology, surveillance, outbreak modelling, health policy, global and environmental health.
scope_out: Individual patient care -> Clinical Medicine; health data infrastructure -> Health Informatics.
example_children: Epidemiology; Global Health; Public Health Surveillance
notes: 20 + 12 + 5 papers plus a COVID-era tail.

scope_in: Health data systems and the delivery of computational tools into care: electronic records, clinical decision support, digital and mobile health, deployment of AI in health settings.
scope_out: A clinical question answered with data -> Clinical Medicine; the ethics of deploying AI -> Responsible AI.
example_children: Digital Health; Clinical Decision Support Systems; Telemedicine
notes: ~60 paper-mentions. Also the home for the generic 'AI in healthcare' family ('Healthcare AI', 'Machine Learning for Healthcare', 'AI for Health'), which is large and otherwise homeless.

scope_in: Research whose subject is non-living matter and energy: astrophysics, fundamental physics, chemistry, materials.
scope_out: Climate, ecosystems and the earth surface -> Environmental Sciences; physics-informed learning as a method -> Scientific Machine Learning; medical radiation physics -> Medical Physics.
example_children: Astrophysics; Computational Chemistry; Materials Science
notes: ~110 paper-mentions. Split from Environmental Sciences deliberately: the two share no methods, no data and no collaborators in this corpus.

scope_in: Astronomical and cosmological objects and surveys: galaxies, black holes, gravitational lensing, telescope and radio data.
scope_out: Neutrino and collider experiments -> Fundamental Physics; satellite imagery of Earth -> Environmental Monitoring.
example_children: Cosmology; Galaxy Evolution; Observational Astrophysics
notes: 15 + 5 + 4 papers plus ~15 tail names including astroinformatics and telescope data analysis.

scope_in: Particle, nuclear, high-energy and quantum physics as research subjects, including detector and simulation work.
scope_out: Astronomical sources -> Astrophysics; physics-informed architectures -> Scientific Machine Learning.
example_children: High Energy Physics; Particle Physics; Neutrino Physics
notes: ~25 paper-mentions. Includes the bare name 'Physics' (5) and quantum mechanics/simulation names.

scope_in: Molecular and atomic systems modelled from chemistry: quantum chemistry, molecular dynamics, reaction and catalyst modelling, cheminformatics.
scope_out: Therapeutic intent -> Drug Discovery; solid-state and device materials -> Materials Science.
example_children: Quantum Chemistry; Molecular Dynamics; Catalysis
notes: 12 + 4 papers plus ~20 tail names. The seam with Drug Discovery is intent, not method, and some names ('Molecular Design') could go either way.

scope_in: Discovery, simulation and characterisation of materials and their properties.
scope_out: Small-molecule chemistry -> Computational Chemistry; manufacturing processes -> Industrial Engineering.
example_children: Materials Discovery; Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials (MLIPs); Crystallography
notes: ~20 paper-mentions spread over 'Material Science', 'Materials Science', 'Materials Modeling', 'Materials Science and Engineering'.

scope_in: Research whose subject is the climate, ecosystems, land surface or agricultural systems.
scope_out: Non-living matter at laboratory or cosmic scale -> Physical Sciences; power generation and grids as engineered systems -> Energy Systems; human health effects of the environment -> Public Health.
example_children: Climate Science; Ecology; Environmental Monitoring
notes: ~80 paper-mentions. Small relative to Biomedical Sciences and that asymmetry is real; it is not to be corrected.

scope_in: The climate system and its projection: emulation of climate models, downscaling, impact assessment, emissions accounting.
scope_out: Ecosystem and species response -> Ecology; grid decarbonisation technology -> Energy Systems.
example_children: Climate Model Emulation; Climate Data Downscaling; Climate Change Impact
notes: ~20 paper-mentions.

scope_in: Organisms, populations and ecosystems: biodiversity, species distributions, conservation, animal behaviour, evolutionary and plant biology.
scope_out: Molecular or clinical biology -> Biomedical Sciences; remote-sensing instruments and imagery -> Environmental Monitoring.
example_children: Biodiversity Monitoring; Species Distribution Modeling; Conservation Biology
notes: ~35 paper-mentions including bioacoustics, trophic and statistical ecology.

scope_in: Observing the earth surface and environment with instruments: remote sensing, aerial and satellite imagery, pollution, fire, seismic and forest monitoring.
scope_out: Image processing methods as such -> Computer Vision; the ecological conclusion drawn -> Ecology.
example_children: Remote Sensing; Forest Change Detection; Fire Monitoring
notes: 11 + 4 papers plus a tail. Added during the tail check: 'Air Pollution', 'Fire Monitoring' and 'Earthquake Monitoring' had no home under a narrower 'Remote Sensing' name.

scope_in: Crops, soils, land use and agricultural production.
scope_out: Plant molecular biology -> Experimental Biology; food-supply logistics -> Industrial Engineering.
example_children: Agricultural Data Analysis; Agriculture and Land Use; Plant Science
notes: Very small (~6 paper-mentions) and retained only because those names genuinely have nowhere else to go. A reviewer may prefer to fold it into Ecology.

scope_in: Research whose subject is a designed artefact or engineered system: robots, software, networks, power systems, vehicles, hardware, industrial operations.
scope_out: The mathematics of control or scheduling -> Formal Foundations of Machine Learning; the infrastructure used to train ML models -> Machine Learning Systems Engineering.
example_children: Robotics; Software Engineering; Energy Systems
notes: ~200 paper-mentions, dominated by software engineering (36) and robotics (25).

scope_in: Embodied agents acting in the physical world: manipulation, locomotion, navigation, SLAM, autonomous vehicles, human-robot interaction, sim-to-real.
scope_out: The learning algorithm named as such -> Reinforcement Learning; stability guarantees for a plant -> Control Theory.
example_children: Robotic Manipulation; Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM); Autonomous Driving
notes: ~70 paper-mentions. Autonomous driving is folded in rather than made a sibling; it is small (5 papers plus a handful) and shares its whole vocabulary with robotics.

scope_in: Building, testing, maintaining and analysing software, including machine learning applied to source code and the engineering of ML-containing systems.
scope_out: Natural-language tasks that happen to use code as text -> Natural Language Processing only if the name says language; verifying neural networks -> Neural Network Verification.
example_children: Software Testing; Program Analysis; Code Generation
notes: 36 papers plus ~60 tail names (fuzzing, technical debt, bug reproducibility, open source, DevOps, requirements). A large and distinctly local cluster.

scope_in: Wireless and wired communication systems: radio access, routing, network optimization, edge and IoT deployment, coding for channels.
scope_out: Communication cost inside a distributed training run -> Federated Learning; graph algorithms as mathematics -> Combinatorial Optimization.
example_children: Wireless Communication; 5G Communications; Software-Defined Networking (SDN)
notes: ~30 paper-mentions.

scope_in: Generation, storage, distribution and consumption of energy: grids, demand response, building energy, renewables, carbon capture.
scope_out: Climate projection -> Climate Science; the energy cost of training models -> Responsible AI.
example_children: Smart Grids; Optimal Power Flow; Demand Response
notes: ~30 paper-mentions including a clear building-energy sub-cluster.

scope_in: Movement of people and goods as a domain: transit networks, traffic control, fleet and crew operations, mobility services.
scope_out: The same problem named as a mathematical instance ('Vehicle Routing Problem') -> Combinatorial Optimization; a self-driving vehicle's perception and control -> Robotics.
example_children: Transportation Research; Public Transport; Traffic Signal Control
notes: ~15 paper-mentions. The split from Combinatorial Optimization on naming rather than substance is deliberate and is one of my least-certain calls.

scope_in: Design and synthesis of computing hardware as the research subject, including neuromorphic and quantum computing devices.
scope_out: Using accelerators to train models faster -> Machine Learning Systems Engineering; quantum mechanics as physics -> Fundamental Physics.
example_children: FPGA Synthesis; VLSI Systems; Neuromorphic Computing
notes: ~12 paper-mentions. Thin but the names are unmistakable and belong nowhere else.

scope_in: Production, manufacturing and the management of industrial and service operations.
scope_out: The scheduling algorithm as mathematics -> Combinatorial Optimization; financial decision making -> Economics.
example_children: Operations Management; Manufacturing; Production Control
notes: ~12 paper-mentions. The weakest category in this branch; retained because the alternative is putting 'Industry 4.0' and 'Revenue Management' in the residual bucket.

scope_in: Research whose subject is people, their minds, their institutions and their interaction with computing systems.
scope_out: The nervous system as the object of study -> Neuroscience; clinical psychiatric care -> Clinical Medicine; ethics and governance of AI specifically -> Responsible AI.
example_children: Human-Computer Interaction; Cognitive Science; Educational Technology
notes: ~120 paper-mentions, dominated by HCI (27). Eight children because the social sciences do not nest; any intermediate grouping here would be invented rather than found.

scope_in: How people use and experience interactive systems: interfaces, usability, human-centred AI, mixed reality, accessibility, creativity support.
scope_out: Recommending items to a user -> Information Retrieval; ethical critique of a deployed system -> Responsible AI.
example_children: Human-Centered AI; Usability; Eye Tracking
notes: 27 papers plus ~40 tail names. Includes visualization and mixed reality, which have no other plausible home in this corpus.

scope_in: Mind and cognition modelled or measured behaviourally: cognitive architectures, theory of mind, reasoning and memory as psychological phenomena.
scope_out: Cognition measured through brain recordings -> Neuroscience; reasoning benchmarks for language models -> Natural Language Processing.
example_children: Cognitive Modeling; Theory of Mind; Cognitive Architecture
notes: ~25 paper-mentions. The seam with Neuroscience is whether the study measures the brain.

scope_in: Behaviour, personality, affect and wellbeing studied as psychological subjects.
scope_out: Psychiatric diagnosis or treatment -> Clinical Medicine; cognitive mechanism modelling -> Cognitive Science.
example_children: Social Psychology; Health Psychology; Behavioral Sciences
notes: ~15 paper-mentions. Close to Cognitive Science; kept separate because the corpus's psychology names are about affect and behaviour, not mechanism.

scope_in: Markets, incentives, finance and economic behaviour as research subjects.
scope_out: Equilibrium mathematics -> Game Theory; operations and revenue management inside a firm -> Industrial Engineering.
example_children: Econometrics; Behavioral Economics; Finance
notes: ~15 paper-mentions.

scope_in: Teaching and learning by people, and the technology built to support it.
scope_out: Medical and surgical training -> Clinical Medicine; curriculum learning for models -> Supervised Learning.
example_children: Educational Technology; Intelligent Tutoring Systems; Educational Data Mining
notes: ~12 paper-mentions. The scope_out against 'Curriculum Learning' matters: that name is a training schedule, not education.

scope_in: Language as an object of linguistic inquiry: syntax, semantics, pragmatics, sociolinguistics, language emergence.
scope_out: Engineering a system that processes text -> Natural Language Processing.
example_children: Computational Linguistics; Sociolinguistics; Syntax
notes: ~15 paper-mentions. Almost every annotator will be tempted to send these to NLP; the distinction is whether the claim is about language or about a system.

scope_in: Computing systems as social phenomena: social media, online communities, collective participation, misinformation and online harm as social problems.
scope_out: The text-classification technique used to detect them -> Natural Language Processing; policy response -> Public Policy.
example_children: Social Media Analytics; Collaborative and Social Computing; Citizen Science
notes: ~15 paper-mentions.

scope_in: Government, regulation and social programmes as research subjects, including programme and impact evaluation.
scope_out: Regulation of AI specifically -> Responsible AI; health policy -> Public Health.
example_children: Public Policy Analysis using AI; Economic Policy Simulation; Child Welfare Systems
notes: ~12 paper-mentions. Overlaps Responsible AI by subject matter; the split is whether AI is the thing being governed.
